_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); electric utility signals on FPL Group's own lines

pit_profile.why: FPL Group, Inc.: 'FPL is a rate-regulated utility engaged primarily in the generation, transmission, distribution and sale of electric energy.' and 'NextEra Energy Resources is FPL Group's competitive energy subsidiary which produces the majority of its electricity from clean and renewable fuels.'; among its risk factors, 'FPL Group and FPL are subject to complex laws and regulations and to changes in laws and regulations as well as changing governmental policies and regulatory actions.', 'Weather affects FPL Group's and FPL's results of operations, as can the impact of severe weather.' and environmental rules 'air quality, water quality, climate change, greenhouse gas emissions, CO2 emissions, waste management, marine and wildlife mortality, natural resources, health, safety and renewable portfolio standards' (its own FY2008 10-K); no disruption theme in the registry is live for an electric utility on this date, so the watch list is empty and the 10-K's words on climate change stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

classification.quality_note: FPL Group, Inc.: 'FPL is a rate-regulated utility engaged primarily in the generation, transmission, distribution and sale of electric energy.' and 'NextEra Energy Resources is FPL Group's competitive energy subsidiary which produces the majority of its electricity from clean and renewable fuels.'; among its risk factors, 'FPL Group and FPL are subject to complex laws and regulations and to changes in laws and regulations as well as changing governmental policies and regulatory actions.', 'Weather affects FPL Group's and FPL's results of operations, as can the impact of severe weather.' and environmental rules 'air quality, water quality, climate change, greenhouse gas emissions, CO2 emissions, waste management, marine and wildlife mortality, natural resources, health, safety and renewable portfolio standards' (its own FY2008 10-K); no disruption theme in the registry is live for an electric utility on this date, so the watch list is empty and the 10-K's words on climate change stay here (the PEP obesity rule). durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 0.55x; +11% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.94; conservative 2yr +14%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -12.6%/yr (worst year FY99-FY08, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +-18.8%/yr (Q3 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +8.3%/yr (FY99-FY08 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +18.2%/yr (best 2-yr run FY99-FY08); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: NEE (retrospective, 2009-11-06) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.55x (27.7% downside to Bear $36 / +50.7% upside to Bull $75) | Adj composite 1.69 vs market 2.63: gap -0.94 [OVERVALUED] | +11% above the EPP floor $45 (11x FY09E $4.07) | Conservative 2-yr case: +14.2% total (+7.1%/yr) | At 12.2x FY09E the 15% hurdle price $66 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; FPL energy sales +0.7% in Q3 2009, forward revenues -17% (no Q4 2009 revenue guide, Q3 2009 revenue as reported); no disruption theme is live for an electric utility on this date.
